fullPassage:
"To grow into a better version of ourselves, we should not stay as we are." That was the first thing our teacher said to us on the first day of school. She wanted us to start the semester by pushing ourselves out of our comfort zones and learning more about ourselves. To help us do so, she gave us an assignment to challenge ourselves in three different ways. The three challenges could involve hobbies, exercise, our studies, or even our relationships. The important part was trying something new for each one. She told us that we should share our experiences with our classmates when we finished the challenges.

Challenge 1: Ticket for One
These days, I tend to watch movies on streaming services. However, if I go to the theater, I usually watch an action or science fiction movie with my friends or family. Those are the kinds of movies they enjoy. Going to the theater alone was something I had never done before. So, for the first challenge, I decided to give it a try. It was nice to choose the movie and the seat on my own. I didn't have to worry about anyone else's preferences. I saw the experience as a good opportunity to watch something different, so I chose a historical drama that I had been curious about. At first, it felt a bit awkward and lonely to sit in the theater by myself. But once the movie started, I became completely absorbed in the story. It was so satisfying just to focus on the movie itself. There was nothing to distract me! This experience made me realize that I sometimes enjoy doing things alone. After the movie, I promised myself that I would try to make my own choices more often and enjoy more activities by myself in the future.

Challenge 2: Riding the Waves
Ever since I was a child, I've always been afraid of water. So I have never enjoyed water activities or felt comfortable while doing them. For the second challenge, I decided to try to overcome this discomfort. However, I wasn't sure what to do at first. One day, I came across a video clip of my cousin surfing at an indoor pool on social media. It looked fun, and I liked the fact that it took place in a shallow pool, not in the ocean. I messaged my cousin about it. She assured me that it wasn't too hard, so I signed up for a beginner course. At the beginning of the lesson, it was hard just to stand up on the board. After some help from the instructor, however, I learned how to balance properly and even managed to surf a few waves! It gave me such a rush of excitement. Being in the water wasn't as bad as I had thought. While the experience didn't completely change my mind about water sports, it did help me discover my sense of adventure.

Challenge 3: A New Look
Of all the challenges I chose for myself, the third one made me the most nervous: changing my hairstyle. For many years, I had kept the same hairstyle because I had been worried about my forehead. I had always thought it was large, and I didn't want to draw attention to it. Since I was feeling confident after the first two challenges, I went to a hair salon and talked to the stylist. He listened to my concerns and helped me find a shorter hairstyle that suited me. The next day at school, my classmates were a bit surprised. But overall, the reactions were positive. I realized that trying a different look wasn't as difficult as I thought it would be. In fact, it made me feel more confident about myself. I didn't expect that stepping out of my comfort zone would have such a positive effect on how I felt about myself.

questions.passage: She wanted us to start the semester by pushing ourselves out of our comfort zones and learning more about ourselves. To help us do so, she gave us an assignment __________ ourselves in three different ways.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] she gave us an assignment to challenge ourselves in three different ways. [해석] 그녀는 세 가지 다른 방식으로 스스로에게 도전하라는 과제를 주었다. [문장4]
det.correct: 명사 assignment를 수식하는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사. assignment to challenge = 도전하라는 과제.
wrongs: ① challenge — 동사원형, 명사 뒤 수식어 역할 불가
② to challenge ✅ — to부정사 형용사적 용법
③ challenging — 현재분사/형용사, 명사 수식 가능하나 '도전적인 과제'가 되어 의미 부적절
④ challenged — 과거분사, 의미 부적절
det.tip:
💡 to부정사의 형용사적 용법
• 명사 + to-V: '~할/~하는' 뜻으로 명사를 뒤에서 수식
• assignment to challenge = 도전할 과제

⚠️ 함정
• challenging은 '도전적인'이라는 뜻의 형용사로 혼동 주의

questions.passage: Going to the theater alone was something I had never done before. So, for the first challenge, I decided to give it a try. It was nice __________ the movie and the seat on my own.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] It was nice to choose the movie and the seat on my own. [해석] 내 스스로 영화와 좌석을 고르는 것이 좋았다. [문장10]
det.correct: It(가주어) was nice to choose(진주어). 가주어-진주어 구문에서 to부정사가 진주어.
wrongs: ① to choose ✅ — It(가주어) + be동사 + 형용사 + to-V(진주어)
② choosing — 가주어 It 구문에서는 to부정사가 자연스러움
③ choose — 동사원형 단독, 문법적으로 불가
④ chosen — 과거분사, 문법적으로 불가
det.tip:
💡 가주어 It 구문
• It is + 형용사 + to-V: to부정사가 진짜 주어
• It was nice to choose = 고르는 것이 좋았다

⚠️ 함정
• It이 대명사인지 가주어인지 구별!

questions.passage: I saw the experience as a good opportunity to watch something different, so I chose a historical drama that I had been curious about. At first, it felt a bit awkward and lonely to sit in the theater by myself. But once the movie started, I became completely __________ in the story.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] I became completely absorbed in the story. [해석] 나는 이야기에 완전히 빠져들었다. [문장14]
det.correct: become + 과거분사(absorbed): 주어(I)가 '흡수되는' 대상이므로 수동/상태 의미의 과거분사.
wrongs: ① absorb — 동사원형, become 뒤 보어로 부적절
② absorbing — 현재분사, '흥미를 끄는' 의미로 사물 주어에 적합
③ absorbed ✅ — 과거분사, '빠져든/몰입한' 상태 (be/become absorbed in)
④ absorption — 명사, become 뒤 보어로 부적절
det.tip:
💡 감정/상태 분사
• absorbed in = ~에 빠져든 (수동→경험자)
• absorbing = 흥미를 끄는 (능동→원인)

⚠️ 함정
• absorbing은 '흥미진진한' 뜻으로 주어가 사물일 때 사용 (The movie was absorbing.)

questions.passage: Ever since I was a child, I've always been afraid of water. So I have never enjoyed water activities or felt comfortable while doing them. For the second challenge, I decided to try __________ this discomfort.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] I decided to try to overcome this discomfort. [해석] 나는 이 불편함을 극복하려고 노력하기로 결심했다. [문장19]
det.correct: decide to try to overcome: decide + to-V, try + to-V 연속 구문. try to do = ~하려고 노력하다.
wrongs: ① overcome — 동사원형 단독, try 뒤에 to 없이 불가
② overcoming — try + -ing는 '시험 삼아 해보다' 의미로, 문맥상 '극복하려고 노력하다'에 부적합
③ overcame — 과거형, try 뒤에 과거형 동사 불가
④ to overcome ✅ — try to do = ~하려고 노력하다
det.tip:
💡 try + to-V vs try + -ing
• try to do = ~하려고 노력하다 (노력/시도)
• try doing = 시험 삼아 해보다 (실험)

⚠️ 함정
• '불편함을 극복하려고 노력' → try to overcome (목적 달성을 위한 노력)

questions.passage: She assured me that it wasn't too hard, so I signed up for a beginner course. At the beginning of the lesson, it was hard just to stand up on the board. After some help from the instructor, however, I learned how __________ properly and even managed to surf a few waves!
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] I learned how to balance properly [해석] 나는 제대로 균형 잡는 법을 배웠다 [문장24]
det.correct: learn how to-V: '~하는 방법을 배우다'. 의문사 how + to부정사 구문.
wrongs: ① balance — 동사원형 단독, how 뒤에 to 필요
② to balance ✅ — how + to-V = ~하는 방법
③ balancing — 동명사, how 뒤에 부적절
④ balanced — 과거분사, how 뒤에 부적절
det.tip:
💡 의문사 + to부정사
• how to do = ~하는 방법
• what to do = 무엇을 할지
• learn/know/tell + 의문사 + to-V 패턴

⚠️ 함정
• how + -ing 형태는 없음!

questions.passage: This experience made me realize that I sometimes enjoy doing things alone. After the movie, I promised myself that I would try to make my own choices more often and enjoy more activities by myself in the future.
questions.stem:
다음 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

This experience ①made me realize that I sometimes enjoy ②doing things alone. After the movie, I promised myself that I would try ③making my own choices more often and enjoy more activities by ④myself in the future.

det.ref: [원문] I would try to make my own choices more often [해석] 더 자주 나만의 선택을 하려고 노력할 것이다 [문장16]
det.correct: ③ making → to make. try to make = ~하려고 노력하다. '시험 삼아 해보다'가 아닌 '노력하다' 의미이므로 to부정사.
wrongs: ① made ✅ — 사역동사 make + 목적어 + 동사원형(realize)
② doing ✅ — enjoy + 동명사(doing)
③ making ❌ — try to make(~하려고 노력하다)가 원문. making은 '시험 삼아 해보다' 의미
④ myself ✅ — 재귀대명사, by myself = 혼자서
det.tip:
💡 try to do vs try doing
• try to do = ~하려고 노력하다 (아직 달성 안 됨)
• try doing = 시험 삼아 해보다 (이미 행동 수행)

⚠️ 함정
• 사역동사 make + O + V원형: made me realize (realize에 to 안 붙음)

questions.passage: For many years, I had kept the same hairstyle because I had been worried about my forehead. I had always thought it was large, and I didn't want __________ attention to it. Since I was feeling confident after the first two challenges, I went to a hair salon and talked to the stylist.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] I didn't want to draw attention to it. [해석] 나는 그것에 주의를 끌고 싶지 않았다. [문장28]
det.correct: want + to부정사. want to draw = ~하기를 원하다.
wrongs: ① to draw ✅ — want + to-V 구문
② drawing — want는 동명사를 목적어로 취하지 않음
③ draw — 동사원형 단독, want 뒤에 to 필요
④ drew — 과거형, want 뒤에 과거형 불가
det.tip:
💡 want + to-V
• want는 to부정사만 목적어로 취한다.
• want doing (❌), want to do (✅)

⚠️ 함정

questions.passage: She wanted us to start the semester by pushing ourselves out of our comfort zones and learning more about ourselves. questions.stem: 위 글에서 밑줄 친 <u>comfort zones</u>의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] pushing ourselves out of our comfort zones [해석] 우리의 안전지대에서 벗어나도록 [문장3]
det.correct: comfort zone = 심리적으로 익숙하고 안전하게 느끼는 영역. 새로운 도전과 대비되는 개념.
wrongs: ① 물리적 장소가 아닌 심리적 영역
② 스트레스 해소와는 무관
③ 친구와의 환경이 아닌 개인의 심리적 영역
④ ✅ 익숙하고 안전하게 느끼는 영역 — pushing out of(벗어나다)와 결합
det.tip:
💡 comfort zone(안전지대/편안한 영역)
• 심리학 용어: 익숙하고 불안감 없이 편안한 상태
• push out of one's comfort zone = 안전지대에서 벗어나다 (= 새로운 도전을 하다)

questions.passage: One day, I came across a video clip of my cousin surfing at an indoor pool on social media. It looked fun, and I liked the fact that it took place in a shallow pool, not in the ocean. I messaged my cousin about it. She assured me that it wasn't too hard, so I signed up for a beginner course.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 밑줄 친 <u>came across</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.ref: [원문] I came across a video clip [해석] 나는 비디오 클립을 우연히 발견했다 [문장20]
det.correct: come across = 우연히 발견하다/마주치다 = happened to find.
wrongs: ① looked for — 의도적으로 찾다 (come across는 우연히)
② happened to find ✅ — 우연히 발견하다
③ passed by — 지나치다 (발견하지 않음)
④ ran into a problem — 문제에 봉착하다 (사물/사람을 만나는 것이 아님)
det.tip:
💡 come across = 우연히 마주치다/발견하다
• 유사 표현: run into, stumble upon, happen to find
• 반의: look for, search for (의도적 탐색)

questions.passage: It gave me such a rush of excitement. Being in the water wasn't as bad as I had thought. __________ the experience didn't completely change my mind about water sports, it did help me discover my sense of adventure.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 연결사로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] While the experience didn't completely change my mind about water sports, it did help me discover my sense of adventure. [해석] 그 경험이 수상 스포츠에 대한 내 생각을 완전히 바꾸지는 못했지만, 모험심을 발견하는 데 도움이 되었다. [문장26]
det.correct: While = ~이지만/~에도 불구하고. 양보의 접속사로 앞뒤 절의 대조적 내용을 연결.
wrongs: ① Because — 인과 관계, 문맥 부적절 ('바꾸지 못했기 때문에 모험심 발견' 논리 불성립)
② Therefore — 결과/결론, 양보 관계에 부적절
③ While ✅ — 양보 '~이지만', 부분적 변화 vs 모험심 발견 대조
④ Moreover — 추가/부연, 대조 관계에 부적절
det.tip:
💡 While의 양보 용법
• While + S + V, S + V = ~이지만 (= Although)
• 앞절: 부정적/제한적 내용 + 뒷절: 긍정적 결과

⚠️ 함정
• While은 '~하는 동안'(시간)과 '~이지만'(양보) 두 의미. 문맥으로 판단!

questions.passage: These days, I tend to watch movies on streaming services. However, if I go to the theater, I usually watch an action or science fiction movie with my friends or family. Those are the kinds of movies they enjoy. Going to the theater alone was something I had never done before. So, for the first challenge, I decided to give it a try. It was nice to choose the movie and the seat on my own. I didn't have to worry about anyone else's preferences. I saw the experience as a good opportunity to watch something different, so I chose a historical drama that I had been curious about.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>Those</u>가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] I usually watch an action or science fiction movie with my friends or family. Those are the kinds of movies they enjoy. [해석] 나는 보통 친구나 가족과 액션이나 공상과학 영화를 본다. 그것들이 그들이 좋아하는 종류의 영화이다. [문장8~9]
det.correct: Those = 바로 앞 문장의 an action or science fiction movie를 지칭. 복수 지시대명사.
wrongs: ① action or science fiction movies ✅ — 앞 문장의 영화 장르를 가리킴
② streaming services — 글의 시작 부분 언급, Those의 직접 선행사 아님
③ the theater — 장소, '종류의 영화'와 연결 불가
④ historical dramas — Those 이후에 나오는 내용
det.tip:
💡 지시대명사 Those
• Those = 앞에서 언급된 복수 명사를 가리킴
• Those are the kinds of movies they enjoy → '그것들'은 액션/SF 영화

questions.passage: After some help from the instructor, however, I learned how to balance properly and even managed to surf a few waves! It gave me such a rush of excitement. Being in the water wasn't as bad as I had thought.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>a rush of excitement</u>의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] It gave me such a rush of excitement. [해석] 그것은 나에게 엄청난 흥분감을 주었다. [문장25]
det.correct: a rush of excitement = 갑자기 밀려오는 흥분감/전율. rush = 갑작스런 강한 감정의 물결.
wrongs: ① 두려움이 아니라 흥분(excitement)
② ✅ 밀려오는 흥분감 — rush = 갑작스런 감정의 파도
③ rush를 '서두르다'로 해석하면 오답. 여기서는 감정의 격류
④ 지속적이 아닌 갑작스러운 감정
det.tip:
💡 rush의 다의어
• rush(명사): ① 서두름 ② 갑작스런 감정의 물결(a rush of ~)
• a rush of excitement/adrenaline = 밀려오는 흥분/아드레날린

questions.passage: He listened to my concerns and helped me find a shorter hairstyle that suited me. The next day at school, my classmates were a bit surprised. But overall, the reactions were positive.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열한 것은?

I realized that trying a different look ( ① as / ② wasn't / ③ difficult / ④ as / ⑤ I thought / ⑥ it would be ).
ch: ② — ③ — ① — ④ — ⑤ — ⑥
② — ① — ③ — ④ — ⑤ — ⑥
② — ③ — ④ — ⑤ — ① — ⑥
② — ① — ③ — ⑤ — ④ — ⑥

det.ref: [원문] trying a different look wasn't as difficult as I thought it would be [해석] 다른 모습을 시도하는 것은 내가 생각했던 것만큼 어렵지 않았다 [문장32]
det.correct: wasn't as difficult as I thought it would be — not as ~ as ... 구문. ② wasn't — ① as — ③ difficult — ④ as — ⑤ I thought — ⑥ it would be.
wrongs: ① ② — ③ — ① — ④ — ⑤ — ⑥: wasn't difficult as as I thought it would be — as 위치 오류
② ② — ① — ③ — ④ — ⑤ — ⑥ ✅: wasn't as difficult as I thought it would be — 원문 일치
③ ② — ③ — ④ — ⑤ — ① — ⑥: wasn't difficult as I thought as it would be — as 위치 오류
④ ② — ① — ③ — ⑤ — ④ — ⑥: wasn't as difficult I thought as it would be — as 사이에 I thought 끼어듦
det.tip:
💡 not as ~ as ... 구문
• wasn't as difficult as I thought it would be
• = 내가 생각했던 것만큼 어렵지 않았다

questions.passage: Ever since I was a child, I've always been afraid of water. So I have never enjoyed water activities or felt comfortable while doing them. For the second challenge, I decided to try to <u>overcoming</u> this discomfort.

det.ref: [원문] I decided to try to overcome this discomfort. [해석] 이 불편함을 극복하려고 노력하기로 결심했다. [문장19]

questions.passage: These days, I tend to watch movies on streaming services. However, if I go to the theater, I usually watch an action or science fiction movie with my friends or family. Those are the kinds of movies they enjoy. Going to the theater alone was something I had never done before. So, for the first challenge, I decided to give it a try. It was nice to choose the movie and the seat on my own. I didn't have to worry about anyone else's preferences. I saw the experience as a good opportunity to watch something different, so I chose a historical drama that I had been curious about. At first, it felt a bit awkward and lonely to sit in the theater by myself. But once the movie started, I became completely absorbed in the story. It was so satisfying just to focus on the movie itself. There was nothing to distract me! This experience made me realize that I sometimes enjoy doing things alone. After the movie, I promised myself that I would try to make my own choices more often and enjoy more activities by myself in the future.

questions.passage:
Ever since I was a child, I've always been afraid of water. So I have never enjoyed water activities or felt comfortable while doing them. For the second challenge, I decided to try to overcome this discomfort. However, I wasn't sure what to do at first. One day, I came across a video clip of my cousin surfing at an indoor pool on social media. It looked fun, and I liked the fact that it took place in a shallow pool, not in the ocean. I messaged my cousin about it. She assured me that it wasn't too hard, so I signed up for a beginner course. At the beginning of the lesson, it was hard just to stand up on the board. After some help from the instructor, however, I learned how to balance properly and even managed to surf a few waves! It gave me such a rush of excitement. Being in the water wasn't as bad as I had thought. While the experience didn't completely change my mind about water sports, it did help me discover my sense of adventure.

Of all the challenges I chose for myself, the third one made me the most nervous: changing my hairstyle. For many years, I had kept the same hairstyle because I had been worried about my forehead. I had always thought it was large, and I didn't want to draw attention to it. Since I was feeling confident after the first two challenges, I went to a hair salon and talked to the stylist. He listened to my concerns and helped me find a shorter hairstyle that suited me. The next day at school, my classmates were a bit surprised. But overall, the reactions were positive. I realized that trying a different look wasn't as difficult as I thought it would be. In fact, it made me feel more confident about myself. I didn't expect that stepping out of my comfort zone would have such a positive effect on how I felt about myself.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로 다음 진술의 T(True) / F(False) 여부를 판단한 것으로 올바른 것은?

(가) 필자는 사촌의 SNS 영상을 보고 실내 수영장에서 서핑을 시도했다.
(나) 서핑 경험을 통해 수상 스포츠에 대한 필자의 생각이 완전히 바뀌었다.
(다) 세 번째 도전 후 반 친구들의 반응은 대체로 긍정적이었다.

det.ref:
[원문] (가) came across a video clip of my cousin surfing at an indoor pool → I signed up for a beginner course (T)
(나) the experience didn't completely change my mind about water sports (F — 완전히 바뀌지는 않았다)
(다) overall, the reactions were positive (T)
det.correct: ② T — F — T: (가) True, (나) False (완전히 바뀌지 않음), (다) True.
wrongs: ① T—T—T: (나)가 F — didn't completely change
② T—F—T ✅
③ F—F—T: (가)가 T — 사촌 영상 보고 신청
④ T—F—F: (다)가 T — reactions were positive
det.tip:
💡 부분 부정 vs 전체 부정
• didn't completely change = 완전히 바꾸지는 못했다 (부분 부정)
• ≠ didn't change at all (전체 부정)
• '완전히 바뀌었다'는 원문과 불일치!
